children: US property and casualty insurer's Q3 net earned premiums rose 1% yr/yr
Q3 net income and non-GAAP operating income per share increased yr/yr
Combined ratio improved to 96.3% from 98.9% on better underwriting and lower loss frequency
Company did not provide specific guidance or outlook for future periods

UNDERWRITING IMPROVEMENT - Co said combined ratio improved due to prior written premium growth earning into revenue and a decrease in losses and loss adjustment expenses, driven by improved loss frequency in private passenger automobile
INVESTMENT INCOME - Co said net investment income rose 15% yr/yr, citing higher assets under management, reinvestment rates above yields on maturing securities, and strong alternative asset returns

PREMIUM TRENDS - Co said net written premiums declined due to a more competitive market and cancellation of underperforming agency relationships, while average written premium per policy increased across major lines due to rate increases
The one available analyst rating on the shares is "hold"
The average consensus recommendation for the property & casualty insurance peer group is "buy."
Wall Street's median 12-month price target for Safety Insurance Group Inc is $49.85, about 52.2% below its November 3 closing price of $104.25
The stock recently traded at 17 times the next 12-month earnings vs. a P/E of 17 three months ago
